# Threadmark — Launch day social

## LinkedIn post

Today we're launching Threadmark.

Threadmark turns folders of research PDFs and notes into a local, searchable map of your evidence. Our first feature is source-linked summaries: each sentence links to the passage behind it, so you can click through and check the claim yourself.

Processing stays on your computer. We don't upload your papers to train anything, and nothing leaves your machine to build the map.

It's for researchers, analysts, and anyone who has ever lost a citation in a folder of PDFs and quietly walked away.

Threadmark is available on Windows and macOS now. A 14-day trial is free; after that it's $12 a month. We're investigating Linux but not yet promising it.

If you have a PDF folder that feels unreadable, that's what we built this for.

## Bluesky post

Threadmark launches today: turn research PDFs and notes into a local, searchable evidence map. Every summary sentence links back to its source passage, so you can click it and read the original. Processing stays on your computer. Windows & macOS now; Linux under investigation. 14-day free trial, then $12/mo.

## Instagram caption

Your research lives in folders of PDFs and notes. Threadmark turns that into a map you can actually search — a map where every sentence in a summary links straight back to the passage it came from.

Click a sentence. See the source. Decide for yourself whether you trust it.

Everything runs locally on your computer. Your papers stay where they are. No upload, no cloud processing.

Threadmark is available on Windows and macOS today. Try it free for 14 days; it's $12 a month after that. Linux is being investigated, but no promises yet.

Bring us your messiest folder.

#research #academicwriting #productivity #tools

## Comment replies

### LinkedIn — "Is this just another chatbot wrapping my documents?"

It isn't — Threadmark doesn't wrap a language model around your documents. There's no chat box and no generated answers. It reads your files on your machine and writes source-linked summaries: every sentence opens the specific passage it came from, so nothing is paraphrased without its citation. If a claim isn't in your corpus, there's no place for it to come from.

### LinkedIn — "Can a university buy seats for a lab?"

Campus or lab licensing isn't something we offer yet. Right now Threadmark is sold as individual subscriptions — $12/month after a 14-day trial — with no seat-based or multi-user purchasing. If you can tell us what a lab deal would need (how many seats, admin billing, access controls), we'll factor that in as we figure out whether team plans make sense. No timeline we can promise today.

### Bluesky — "no linux, no deal"

Understood. Linux is genuinely being investigated, but we won't promise it until it's ready. If it ships, we'll announce it plainly — no countdowns, no waitlists.

### Bluesky — "Does local mean you train on my papers anyway?"

No. "Local" means all processing happens on your computer and your PDFs don't leave it to run Threadmark. We don't train anything on your papers, and the summaries are produced from your own documents, not learned from them.

### Instagram — "I paid and the app has been stuck indexing for two hours."

That isn't how indexing should behave, and we're sorry you hit it. A good first step: quit the app, reopen it, and try indexing one small folder on its own to see if it still stalls. If it does, please reach out to us through the app's support link so we can look at the logs on your machine — we won't ask you to share account or billing details here.

### Instagram — "Would this work for a literature review in Japanese?"

We've built and tested Threadmark around English-language sources, so we can't promise how it will handle Japanese. Search and summarization are tuned for English, and Japanese support isn't something we've validated. If you run the 14-day trial on Japanese PDFs, we'd genuinely like to know what works and where it falters.

# Voice choices

Precise: we state exactly what Threadmark does (source-linked summaries, local processing) and name the price, trial, and platforms rather than leaning on adjectives.

Warm: launch posts speak directly to researchers and end with an invitation, not a slogan.

Mildly nerdy, never grandiose: we call the product what it is — a searchable evidence map — and avoid words like "revolutionary" or "AI-powered."

import re

bs = section('Bluesky post')
ig = section('Instagram caption')

body = ig.split('\n\n')[:-1]

EOF
